catalog_entry.label: CFB half-time/full-time double result
catalog_entry.target: Probability of a stated (1st-half result, full-game result) pair, half ties allowed, full game incl. OT.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Each market is one cell of a nine-cell partition: first-half result (team A leads, tie, team B leads) crossed with the full-game winner, which always exists because overtime is included. The cell probability is P(half state) times P(full winner | half state). The first factor comes from a lumpy half-margin distribution built from the strength gap, team half-scoring splits and possession order; the second comes from second-half and overtime play given the half state, where leaders slow down, trailing teams take risk, starters are pulled in blowouts, and the side kicking off to open the game receives the second-half kickoff. Reversal cells (half leader loses) and tie-at-half cells carry the mass a product of marginals misprices.

inputs.why: Non-market composite rating sets the full-game expected margin from which both half and full-game outcome probabilities are built.
Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency shows how quickly each side scores early, which shapes the half-margin spread around the strength gap.
Opponent-adjusted defensive efficiency completes the per-drive scoring rates used for both halves of the joint simulation.
Confirmed starting QB at decision time moves both the half and full-game margin; a backup changes the reversal likelihood too.
Team-specific first versus second half scoring shares (fast starters, late surgers) move the half margin away from half the full margin.
Discrete half-margin mass at 0 and key numbers gives the half-tie leg (Tie 1H) its probability, which a normal approximation misstates.
For the tie-at-half cells, P(team wins | tied half) is the second factor of the joint and is not the unconditional win probability.
Nine-cell conditional of full-game winner given half bucket and rating gap; the core joint-dependence input of this contract.
Who receives the opening kick decides who gets the extra first-half drive and the second-half kickoff, linking half and second-half margins.
End-of-half drives decide many half leads and ties because they occur after the clock budget is already partly used.
Starter removal with big second-half leads caps reversals in mismatches and truncates margin growth after halftime.
Trailing teams speed up and leaders slow down after halftime, which changes the number of second-half drives available for a comeback.
Aggressive fourth-down policy raises second-half variance for the trailing side, fattening the reversal cells.
Full-game result includes overtime, so tied regulation games must be resolved by the college OT format into a winner.
Converts a regulation tie into a full-game winner probability through alternating-possession OT scoring.
Home field shifts both halves; neutral sites (bowls, CFP) remove it and change the tie-at-half winner tilt.
Wind and rain lower scoring, which raises half-tie mass and compresses margins in both halves.
Tests whether staff identity tilts reversals after halftime beyond the rating gap; heavily shrunk.
The rules define the cell pair (half result incl. tie, full game incl. OT) and the 48-hour postponement clause.
Settled result per cell is needed to verify the nine-cell partition sums to one on Kalshi's settlement.

interactions.hypothesis: A half lead protects less when the leader is the weaker team: reversal probability rises with the pre-game gap against the half leader.
Wind or rain lowers half scoring and raises the zero-margin mass, enlarging every Tie 1H cell non-linearly.
Starter removal after a large half lead truncates second-half margin and pushes reversal cells toward zero beyond what rate models imply.
The team deferring to receive the second-half kickoff converts a tied or one-score half into an extra drive, shifting tie-to-win cells toward it.

contract.settlement_definition: Each KXNCAAF1HFT market names a pair: a 1st-half result (one team leads, or the 1st half is tied) and a full-game winner, with the full game including overtime. YES only if both legs are correct; any other combination is NO. Because overtime is included the full-game leg has no tie, so the series partitions into nine cells per game (3 half states x 2 winners, with the tie cells taking both winners). If the game is postponed but starts within 48 hours it settles on the official final; beyond 48 hours the sampled text is truncated ('resolve to a fai...'), so the exact fallback (likely a fair-price settlement) cannot be read. The settlement data source is not visible in the sample.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on the combination of the 1st half and full game (including overtime) result
rules_evidence.establishes: Both legs are combined and the full-game leg includes overtime, so the full-game leg never ties.

rules_evidence.quote: If either the first half or full game result is incorrect, the market resolves to No as both results have to be correct in order for the market to resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Conjunction settlement: a single wrong leg gives NO; there is no partial payout or push.

rules_evidence.quote: If Notre Dame and Miami (FL) tie in the 1st half and Notre Dame wins the full game
rules_evidence.establishes: A tied first half is an explicit leg value, so tie-at-half cells exist and need half-tie mass.

variants_and_edge_cases: Tie-at-half cells: the half leg can be a tie (e.g. 'Tie 1H / Notre Dame game'), so the half margin's mass at exactly zero matters, including 0-0 halves.
Overtime: full game includes OT, so a regulation tie is not a NO for both winner cells; one of the two tie-in-regulation paths resolves via the college OT format.
Postponement: game starting within 48 hours of original time stays open and settles on the official final; the beyond-48-hours outcome text is truncated in the sample.
Only one series with one sampled market; it is unknown whether every game lists all nine cells or only a subset (matters for coherence checks across cells).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final and half-time score of the game; the sampled rules do not name the source agency (truncated), so the resolving provider is unverified.

mechanism.summary: The outcome is a pair drawn from the joint law of (first-half margin, final margin after overtime). Start from team strength to get expected margin and total. Split expected scoring into halves using team-specific half shares and possession order; the half margin is a discrete, lumpy variable with real mass at zero in close, low-total games. The second half is then played conditional on the half state: leaders shorten the game, trailing teams pass and go for it on fourth down, starters come out in blowouts, and the team that deferred gets the second-half kickoff. Regulation ties go to college overtime with alternating possessions and two-point shootouts from the third OT. The joint therefore has positive dependence (half leaders usually win) with reversal tails that depend on the strength gap and script, which independence of halves misprices.

stages.name: Full-game strength gap and scoring environment
stages.description: Non-market team ratings, opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency, confirmed quarterbacks and venue set the expected final margin and total. These two numbers determine how often a half is close enough to tie and how large half leads tend to be, and are the conditioning variables for reversal rates in the second half.
stages.distribution: Expected margin is continuous but final margins are fat-tailed with key-number clustering at 3, 7, 10 and 14.

stages.name: First-half margin with tie mass
stages.description: First-half margin comes from roughly five to seven drives per team: team half-scoring shares (fast starters versus slow starters), who gets the opening kickoff and the extra drive, scripted openers and the end-of-half two-minute drive. The result is a lattice of 3- and 7-point steps with a material probability of exactly zero, highest when the expected margin is small and the total low or weather suppresses scoring.
stages.distribution: Discrete lattice with spikes at 0, +/-3, +/-7; tie mass roughly 6-12 percent in close games, smaller in mismatches.

stages.name: Second half conditional on the half state
stages.description: Given the half margin, the second half changes regime: leaders run the ball and slow the clock, trailing teams pass and go for it on fourth down, large leads trigger starter removal, and the side that deferred receives the second-half kickoff. These behaviours set the reversal probability (half leader loses) and the winner split after a tied half, which together are the off-diagonal cells of the nine-cell table.
stages.distribution: Conditional win probability is sigmoid in half margin, shifted by pregame gap; reversal tails thin out quickly beyond two scores.

stages.name: Overtime resolution of regulation ties
stages.description: Because the full game includes overtime, regulation ties are converted into a winner through the college format: alternating possessions from the 25, mandatory two-point tries from the second OT and two-point shootouts from the third. Kicking and red-zone offence tilt the winner away from 50/50, and the probability of reaching OT depends on the regulation tie curve, which is linked to the half state.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli winner with mild skill tilt; reached in a few percent of games, more in close low-total matchups.

stages.name: Settlement of the cell
stages.description: The market pays only if both legs match. The partition identity (all nine cells sum to one) is a hard coherence constraint, a postponement within 48 hours keeps the market alive, and beyond 48 hours the sampled fallback wording is cut off. Settlement depends on the official half-time and final score, with overtime counted for the full-game leg only.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from (half margin sign, final winner) to YES/NO; rare void path on cancellation.

cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.label: Half-time state to full-game winner transition matrix
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.mechanism: Conditional probability that each side wins the full game (overtime included) given the first-half margin bucket and the pre-game non-market rating gap; the off-diagonal cells (leader at half loses) are the reversal mass.
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.rationale: The double result needs the joint of half and full-game outcomes, and reversals are not the product of two marginals: a 10-point half lead by a 14-point underdog is less safe than the same lead by a favourite, and in CFB the trailing team keeps receiving the second-half kickoff about half the time. Independence over-prices favourite/favourite and under-prices underdog-leads/favourite-wins cells.
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.measurement: FBS games 2014 onward with quarter line scores. Half margin buckets: <=-15, -14..-8, -7..-4, -3..-1, 0, 1..3, 4..7, 8..14, >=15 (team perspective). Pre-game rating gap from own non-market rating (SP+-style) in 4-point bins plus home/neutral flag and second-half receiver indicator. Fit an ordered logistic of P(win full game | half bucket, gap) with a smooth in gap; shrink each cell toward a bivariate-normal-of-halves baseline with prior strength 60 games. Output nine cells per game; as-of last completed game before kickoff.
raw_data: games: game_id, season, week, home, away, neutral_site
line_scores: points by quarter per team
own rating vintages: team, week, rating
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.why: Directly produces the nine joint cells KXNCAAF1HFT settles on, including the reversal cells that marginal half and full-game models cannot generate.

cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.label: Coach second-half minus first-half efficiency differential
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.mechanism: Persistent tendency of a staff to improve (or fade) after halftime, measured as second-half minus first-half opponent-adjusted EPA per play, net of score-state effects.
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.rationale: Reputed halftime adjusters shift the reversal cells; most of the raw differential is noise and garbage-time contamination, so it must be measured only in competitive states and shrunk hard. Included as a test of whether staff identity moves the half-to-full transition beyond rating gap.
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.measurement: Per head coach and coordinator pair, last 3 seasons: mean (2H - 1H) offensive plus defensive EPA/play from CFBD plays, restricted to plays with win probability 0.10-0.90, opponent-adjusted by opponent season EPA allowed; shrink toward 0 with prior strength 25 games; reset partially (50 percent) on coordinator change. Units: EPA/play; as-of the prior Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD plays with EPA and win probability (free key)
raw_data: plays: game_id, period, offense, defense, ppa/epa, pre-snap win probability
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.why: Would tilt reversal cells (trailing at half, wins game) for specific staffs; expected to be small after shrinkage and kept as context.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: Non-market rating is the anchor of the full-game expected margin; the joint cells are centred on it rather than on a line.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Adds per-drive scoring speed beyond the composite; partly redundant with sp_plus, so secondary rather than primary for this joint.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Same reasoning as offence; mostly absorbed in the composite, but needed for per-half drive simulation.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: A late QB change moves every one of the nine cells; timestamped vintages are required because the contract trades through kickoff.

cfb.half_split.reason: Directly allocates expected points between halves; team-specific allocation drives the half leg separately from the full leg.

cfb.period_margin_lattice.reason: Supplies the discrete half-margin mass at zero needed for every Tie 1H cell.

cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.reason: Exactly the conditional factor of the tie-at-half cells; it was written for this series and fits it.

cfb.period_possession_allocation.reason: Opening-kick order shifts the half margin by a fraction of a point and links halves; the toss is unknown pregame, so probabilistic only.

cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.reason: End-of-half scoring decides close half results; matters most for the half-tie and one-score half cells.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Caps margin growth after halftime and so lowers reversal probability in mismatches; affects cells where the favourite leads at half.

cfb.state_dependent_pace.reason: Score-state tempo changes the number of second-half drives a trailing team gets; a mechanism of reversal mass.

cfb.fourth_down_aggression.reason: Raises variance of the trailing side's second half; effect real but small relative to the rating gap.

cfb.ot_model.reason: The rules include overtime in the full-game result, so regulation ties must be mapped into a winner; without OT the partition is wrong.

cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.reason: Refines the OT winner split beyond 50/50 using offensive and kicking strength; small share of games reach OT.

cfb.venue.reason: Home advantage shifts both halves and the tie-at-half winner tilt; removed at neutral postseason sites.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Low-scoring weather raises half-tie mass; only matters for a minority of games with strong wind or rain.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the two legs, OT inclusion and the truncated postponement clause; versioned capture is needed.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Not predictive; used to check settlement of each cell and the partition identity.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that the half leader holds on depends on who leads: a 7-point half lead by a 17-point favourite converts at very high rates, the same lead by an underdog converts far less often because the stronger team gets more second-half scoring drives. The reversal cell is a function of half margin and gap jointly, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit win|half margin with and without a half-margin x rating-gap term on 2014+ FBS games; compare log loss on held-out seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Sustained wind above about 15 mph and heavy rain lower first-half scoring; the probability of a tied half rises faster than linearly as expected half total falls toward 14 because 0-0, 3-3 and 7-7 halves become common.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin games by kickoff wind and precipitation; compare observed half-tie frequency against a lattice fitted without weather, by expected-total bin.

interactions.mechanism: Once the half lead exceeds about three scores, backups enter during the third quarter and the leader stops scoring, but the trailing team also faces a large deficit; reversal cells collapse to near zero above that threshold while margin cells become unreliable.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot P(reversal) by half margin with a change-point fit; check whether the drop location differs for coaches with early versus late starter pull.

interactions.mechanism: After a tied half, the team receiving the second-half kickoff gets the first and often an extra possession; its conditional win probability is higher than the opponent's at equal strength, so the two tie-at-half cells split unevenly by who deferred.
interactions.how_to_test: Among halves tied at the break, regress full-game win on second-half receiver indicator plus rating gap and home flag.

interactions.mechanism: A trailing team that both speeds up and goes for it on fourth down raises second-half variance on two axes; the comeback probability scales with the product of extra drives and per-drive upside, so an aggressive up-tempo underdog fattens reversal cells far more than either trait alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact trailing-team second-half seconds per play with fourth-down go rate in the reversal model; compare to main-effects-only fit.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic in half margin, steepest between -7 and +7
nonlinearities.why: Each additional point of half lead is worth most when the half is within one score; beyond 15 points win probability saturates near one, so reversal cells are concentrated in one-score halves.

nonlinearities.shape: spike at zero decaying with absolute expected margin
nonlinearities.why: Half-tie probability falls sharply as the expected half margin moves away from zero and also as expected half total rises, so Tie 1H cells are much more valuable in close low-scoring games than a linear rule suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: step: regulation tie maps to one winner
nonlinearities.why: The overtime inclusion turns a regulation tie into a full-game win for one side, adding a discrete chunk of probability to the two winner cells that is absent if OT were excluded.

catalog_entry.label: College football pre-packaged parlays (multi-game moneyline and same-game combos)
contract_types: MVE NCAAF Pre Pack (same-game spread + total)
catalog_entry.target: Probability that every leg of a pre-packaged combination resolves YES jointly: several named teams all win their games, or a spread cover and a total side in the same game both hit.
catalog_entry.mechanism: A pack pays only if every leg hits, so its probability is the joint of leg events, not a single game outcome. For multi-game moneyline packs each leg is a game winner (always decided via overtime); legs are close to independent in game noise but share rating-model error, especially conference offsets in cross-conference postseason games, plus slate-wide shocks such as opt-out waves and weather. For same-game packs the legs (spread cover and total side) are strongly dependent through pace and score state: underdog cover pairs with the under, favourite cover with the over. Errors in each leg compound multiplicatively, so calibration of every leg and of the dependence matters more than in a single-game market.

inputs.why: Non-market strength for each leg's team pair is the base of every leg probability in the pack.
Opponent-adjusted offence sets both the margin and the total of a same-game leg pair.
Opponent-adjusted defence completes the per-leg expected margin and total.
Postseason legs pit conferences that rarely meet; mis-set conference offsets bias several legs in the same direction.
Joint rating draws carry shared uncertainty across the teams in a slate, the source of cross-leg correlation.
Leg-pair correlation matrix for multi-game moneyline packs, replacing the independence assumption.
Joint margin-total probability at the spread and total strikes of a same-game pack.
A starting QB change in any leg moves that leg and so the whole conjunction; postseason QB opt-outs and transfers are common.
Bowl and CFP opt-outs of draft-bound starters change leg strength right before the game and can hit several legs at once.
Postseason layoffs differ by team (first-round byes versus teams that played the week before), affecting legs unevenly.
CFP first-round games are on campus while later rounds are neutral; home field is present in some legs and absent in others.
Combined possessions set the total leg of a same-game pack and widen margin variance.
Wind and rain lower totals in the same-game pack and add a shared shock to outdoor legs on one date.
Starter removal truncates margins, shaping the joint tail of a favourite-cover plus over combination.
Moneyline legs always have a winner via OT; whether OT points count for spread and total legs is not stated in the sampled rules.
Portal-heavy rosters make prior-season data a weaker guide; matters for early-season packs and for postseason roster churn.
Leg list, strikes and the absent void/postponement wording come only from the per-market rules text.
Postponement or cancellation of one leg's game, and how the pack is handled, depends on lifecycle events.

interactions.hypothesis: When several legs pit the same conference against others, an error in that conference offset moves all legs together and raises the all-win and all-lose probabilities.
Underdog-cover-and-under dependence is strongest when the expected margin sits near the spread strike and weak for large mismatches.
Opt-outs add leg-specific strength loss with wide uncertainty; in postseason packs this inflates posterior spread per leg and the joint tail.

contract.settlement_definition: Each MVE NCAAF Pre Pack market lists two to four legs and resolves YES only if every listed leg happens: for KXNCAAFPREPACK2ML/3ML/4ML each named team must win its named game (games 'originally scheduled' on given dates); for KXNCAAFPREPACKSGP a named team must cover a half-point spread and the combined score must be on the named side of a half-point total in one game. The sampled markets have empty rules_secondary, so overtime inclusion for spread/total legs, postponement windows, cancellation of one leg's game and the settlement source are not stated. Half-point strikes rule out pushes; moneyline legs cannot tie because CFB games go to overtime.

variants_and_edge_cases: Leg count varies (2, 3, 4) and legs can span different dates; a 4-leg pack is open across Dec 31 and Jan 1 games, so partial information arrives before the last leg.
Same-game pack legs are a spread and a total; overtime inclusion for these legs is not stated in the sampled text (empty rules_secondary).
No void or postponement wording is visible: if one leg's game is cancelled or moved, it is unknown whether the pack voids, settles at fair value, or treats the leg as lost.
Phrase 'originally scheduled for' anchors legs to a scheduled game date, implying a postponement clause exists elsewhere that was not sampled.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final scores of each leg's game; the sampled rules do not name the resolving agency (rules_secondary empty), so the source is unverified.

mechanism.summary: A pre-pack is a conjunction. For moneyline packs, the outcome is the product of each named team winning, adjusted for dependence: game noise is independent across games, but the estimate of every leg uses the same rating model, and postseason slates feature cross-conference games where conference offsets are poorly identified, so model error is shared; opt-out waves before bowls and common weather add slate shocks. For the same-game pack, the spread and total legs come from one bivariate score distribution where pace, script and blowout truncation tie margin to total. Leg probabilities multiply, so a small bias in each compounds across three or four legs, and the conjunction is most sensitive to the least likely leg. Contract mechanics add a layer: legs settle at different times and the void handling for a moved game is not stated.

stages.name: Per-leg game winner or cover probability
stages.description: For each named game, non-market ratings, opponent-adjusted efficiency, confirmed quarterback, venue (campus CFP first round versus neutral later rounds) and postseason layoff give the probability that the named team wins or covers. Because CFB games always produce a winner through overtime, moneyline legs have no tie branch, which simplifies each leg to a single Bernoulli.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per leg; win probability is a sigmoid in rating gap with fat margin tails in mismatches.

stages.name: Cross-game dependence of legs
stages.description: Leg outcomes in different games share the rating model's errors. In bowl and CFP slates, teams from two or three power conferences meet each other after a season with few cross-conference games, so conference offsets are uncertain; if one conference is over-rated, every leg backing it fails together. Opt-out waves and slate weather add common shocks. The joint therefore has more mass on all-hit and all-miss than the product of marginals.
stages.distribution: Weak positive correlation per leg pair (driven by shared offsets); joint tails heavier than independence implies, growing with leg count.

stages.name: Within-game margin-total joint for same-game packs
stages.description: For a spread-plus-total pack, possessions, efficiency and score state jointly produce margin and total. Low-possession, low-efficiency games compress margins (helping the underdog +7.5) and stay under; blowouts push margin and total up together until starters are pulled. The joint pmf at the half-point strikes, with key-number lumps near 7 and 3, is what pays.
stages.distribution: Bivariate lattice pmf of (margin, total) with correlation sign depending on the favoured side; key-number spikes.

stages.name: Conjunction, timing and settlement
stages.description: The pack pays one dollar only if all legs hit. Legs in multi-date packs resolve sequentially, and the sampled rules carry no void or overtime wording for spread and total legs, so the treatment of a moved or cancelled leg game and of overtime points is unknown. Overtime itself guarantees moneyline legs a winner under the college format.
stages.distribution: Product (with dependence) of Bernoulli legs; sensitivity of the pack to leg i equals the joint probability of the other legs.

cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.label: Cross-game dependence of leg outcomes through shared rating error
cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.mechanism: Correlation of game-result residuals across different games on the same slate caused by shared model error (one conference over- or under-rated), common postseason conditions (layoff length, opt-out waves) and shared weather.
cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.rationale: Separate games look independent, so the parlay price is usually the product of leg probabilities; but if a rating model systematically over-rates one conference, all legs on that conference's teams fail together. In CFP slates with three or four legs involving SEC/Big Ten teams, this common error dominates the joint error even when game noise is independent.
cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.measurement: From joint posterior draws of team ratings (shared conference offsets kept), compute for each pair of legs the correlation of win indicators across draws; validate empirically by the correlation of signed residuals (actual margin minus non-market expected margin) between games on the same date that share a conference, 2014+ postseason and late regular season, shrunk toward zero with prior strength 200 game pairs. Output a leg-pair correlation matrix for the slate; as-of last completed game.

cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.why: Turns a product of marginals into a correct joint for 2-, 3- and 4-leg moneyline packs; omitted it understates the probability of all-favourite and all-underdog outcomes.

cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.label: Within-game joint pmf of margin and total at contract strikes
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.mechanism: Bivariate distribution of final margin and combined points in one game, given non-market expected margin and expected total, evaluated at the half-point spread and total strikes of a same-game pack.
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.rationale: A same-game pack such as 'underdog +7.5 and under 48.5' pays on a correlated pair: low-scoring games have compressed margins, so an underdog cover and an under are positively dependent; a favourite cover and an over are positively dependent through blowouts. The dependence changes with the strength gap and with key numbers near 7 and 3.
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.measurement: FBS games 2014+: bin by non-market expected margin (3-point bins) and expected total (5-point bins); estimate the joint empirical pmf of (margin, total) on integer lattice with a bivariate kernel smoother centred on a drive-level simulation prior (prior strength 150 games per cell). Evaluate P(margin > -k and total < t) for half-point strikes; report the ratio to the product of marginals as the dependence factor. Overtime points included unless the rules exclude them; as-of kickoff.

own expected margin and total vintages
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.why: The only input that prices KXNCAAFPREPACKSGP correctly; marginal spread and total models multiplied together misprice it.

interactions.mechanism: In the sampled 3- and 4-leg packs, SEC and Big Ten teams appear in most legs. If the conference offset is wrong by a few points, each leg moves the same direction, so the probability that all named favourites win is higher than the product when the offset is overstated and lower when understated; the effect grows with legs sharing a conference.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test postseason slates: compare realised all-leg hit rates of conference-concentrated versus mixed combinations against product-of-marginal forecasts.

interactions.mechanism: With few expected possessions, scoring variance shrinks for both margin and total, so an underdog +7.5 and under 48.5 become strongly positively dependent; with many possessions the margin variance grows while the under is unlikely, and the dependence weakens.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the joint-to-product ratio of (dog cover, under) by expected-possessions tercile on historical games.

interactions.mechanism: For favourite-cover-plus-over combinations, the joint grows with the strength gap until the favourite's lead triggers starter removal; beyond that point the total stalls while margin is capped, so the joint flattens.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot P(fav cover and over) against expected margin and fit a change-point near the starter-pull lead size.

interactions.mechanism: Losing a starting QB or several draft-bound starters reduces leg win probability proportionally; because the pack multiplies legs, the pack price falls by the same factor, and simultaneous news on two legs compounds.
interactions.how_to_test: In finalized postseason packs, compare predicted pack probabilities using pregame-confirmed versus season-default starters against settlement.

interactions.mechanism: Long postseason layoffs (three to five weeks) add uncertainty to team strength that is absent in the regular season, so posterior spread per leg widens and the pack's distribution moves toward the extremes in postseason regimes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare residual variance of postseason versus regular-season games for teams with 21+ day layoffs.

nonlinearities.shape: sigmoid per leg, multiplied across legs
nonlinearities.why: Pack probability is a product of sigmoids in rating gaps; a one-point error in the weakest leg's gap moves the pack more than the same error in a heavy-favourite leg because that leg's sigmoid slope is steepest near even odds.

nonlinearities.shape: lumpy at key numbers 3 and 7 around the +7.5 strike
nonlinearities.why: Final margins cluster at exactly 7 and 3, so moving the spread strike from 6.5 to 7.5 changes the cover leg by a jump, and the joint with the total inherits that step.

catalog_entry.label: CFB season stat leader
contract_types: College Football Big Ten Stats Leaders
catalog_entry.target: Probability that a named player finishes the regular season as the leader of a stated counting stat (rushing yards, receiving yards, passing touchdowns, sacks) in a conference or in Division I, with ties paying $1/N.
catalog_entry.mechanism: A leader market is an order statistic: each eligible player's end-of-regular-season total equals the current total plus remaining production, and YES requires the named player's total to be the maximum. Remaining production is games remaining (byes, Hawaii exemption, cancellations; conference title games excluded) times participation times volume share of team plays times efficiency against remaining opponents, with overdispersed game-to-game variation. Teammates compete for the same carries or targets; QB health links receivers to passers; sacks depend on opponents' dropbacks. Late in the season the current gap dominates; early, usage and health do. Ties pay $1/N, which matters for small-integer stats.

inputs.why: Current regular-season totals, gap to rivals and remaining-game count for each candidate; the state the race is simulated from.
Order-statistic simulation over the whole field including unlisted players and teammates competing for usage.
Carry, target and snap shares decide how much of the team's volume each rushing or receiving candidate gets.
Pass-rush snaps and sack rate per snap drive the SEC sacks race; offence inputs say nothing about it.
A missed game removes a full game of production and a season-ending injury ends the race; the rules also void to NO if the player does not play.
Team rush attempts given expected script set the volume pool for a rushing-yards leader.
Team dropbacks given script set volume for passing-TD and receiving-yards leaders.
Sacks need opponent dropbacks; facing pass-heavy opponents raises a pass rusher's sack chances.
Touchdowns per scoring trip and the pass/rush split decide passing TD accumulation for a QB.
Yards per carry and explosive-run rate scale rushing-yards accumulation per opportunity.
Remaining opponents' allowed rushing, receiving and sack rates adjust per-game projections.
Stars on dominant teams sit in fourth quarters of blowouts, cutting volume despite strong teams.
A receiving or passing leader depends on the starting QB staying healthy; a backup lowers passing production.
Overdispersed game-level production and long-run tails decide how fast a trailing candidate can catch up.
Tie probability at the top for discrete stats determines the $1/N payout share.
Late-season redshirt or draft-related sit-outs remove remaining regular-season games.
November wind and snow suppress passing and favour rushing volume in remaining outdoor games.
Regular-season scope, conference-title-game exclusion, play-in-conference requirement and $1/N tie payout come from the rules.
Stat corrections and definitions (college sacks counted as rushing losses, half sacks) differ between providers and the official record.

interactions.hypothesis: A missed game costs the leader more when the gap to second place is smaller than one game's expected production.
Stars on dominant teams get high per-game share but lose fourth-quarter snaps, so strong team quality helps volume up to a point and then hurts it.
Sack accumulation scales with the product of pass-rush rate and opponent dropbacks; a rusher facing run-heavy opponents loses ground.

contract.settlement_definition: YES if the named player records the most of the stated stat (passing TDs in the ACC, receiving yards in the Big 12, rushing yards in the Big Ten, sacks in the SEC, rushing yards in Division I) over the 2026 regular season. All regular-season games count including non-conference games; conference championship games are excluded (and so are bowls and CFP, which are postseason). If the player does not play in the conference (or in the regular season for the national series) for any reason, NO. Ties at the top pay YES $1/N rounded down to the cent, NO 1 minus that. The sampled text is truncated before the source-of-truth clause, so the stat provider is not visible.

rules_evidence.quote: All regular season games count towards this market, regardless of whether the game is within conference. Conference championship games are not included in the regular season.
rules_evidence.establishes: Scope is the full regular season including non-conference games; conference title games do not add to totals.

rules_evidence.quote: If John Neider does not play in the Big 12 in the 2026 regular season for any reason, the market for that player resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: A player who never plays in the conference settles NO, not void, so participation risk is a NO risk.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are tied for the most rushing yards at the end of the regular season, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent)
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties split the payout 1/N, so tie probability is part of fair value.

rules_evidence.quote: If Markell Holman records the most rushing yards in Division I college football in the 2026 college football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: National series is 'Division I', which may include FCS players, unlike conference series scoped to one conference.

rules_evidence.quote: If Nick Rinaldi records the most sacks in the Southeastern Conference in the 2026 college football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Defensive stat series (sacks), where official half sacks make the stat a 0.5 lattice with real tie mass.

variants_and_edge_cases: Stat type varies by series (passing TDs, receiving yards, rushing yards, sacks); each has a different volume driver and tie mass.
National series says 'Division I', which could include FCS players; conference series are limited to conference members.

Unequal game counts: teams with a Hawaii road game may play 13 regular-season games, teams with cancelled games fewer; conference title games excluded even though they are 'extra' games for top teams.
Player must 'play in' the conference; a player who plays zero snaps resolves NO, but partial seasons count normally.
College stat conventions: sacks count as rushing yards lost for QBs, sacks are recorded in half units; post-game stat corrections can change totals.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official regular-season statistics; the sampled rules are truncated before the source clause, so whether Kalshi uses NCAA official stats, conference stats or a provider (ESPN) is unverified.

mechanism.summary: The leader is the maximum of many players' season totals, so the named player's probability depends on his current total, the field's totals, and the distribution of everyone's remaining production. Remaining production is a product: regular-season games left (schedule, byes, cancellations; title games excluded) times probability of playing each game times opportunity volume (team plays times usage share for backs and receivers, dropbacks and red-zone trips for passing TDs, opponent dropbacks times pass-rush snaps for sacks) times per-opportunity efficiency against the remaining opponents, with fourth-quarter volume lost in blowouts. Game-level production is overdispersed (long runs, multi-sack games), teammates share volume, and players on one team share pace and QB shocks. With a few weeks left the race is mostly the current gap plus injury risk; the 1/N tie rule adds value for discrete stats.

stages.name: Current leaderboard and games remaining
stages.description: As of the query week, each contender has a regular-season total and a count of remaining regular-season games, which differs by team because byes fall in different weeks, a Hawaii road trip allows a 13th game and cancelled games are not replaced; conference title games do not count. The gap to the leader measured in expected games of production is the main state variable in November.
stages.distribution: Deterministic current totals; games remaining is a small integer (0-5 in November) per team.

stages.name: Participation and health
stages.description: Each remaining game requires the player to be available. Running backs and edge rushers carry higher per-game injury risk than quarterbacks; draft prospects on eliminated teams sometimes sit late games, and a never-played player resolves NO. A receiver's or passer's production also depends on the starting quarterback staying healthy. Lost games shift the whole remaining total down in game-sized steps.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with position-specific rates; season-ending injury is an absorbing state giving zero remaining production.

stages.name: Opportunity volume per game
stages.description: Volume is stat-specific: carries for rushing leaders (team rush attempts under expected script times carry share), targets for receivers (team dropbacks times target share), red-zone trips and pass share for passing touchdowns, and opponent dropbacks times pass-rush snaps for sacks. Stars on dominant teams lose fourth-quarter snaps in blowouts, while trailing teams pass more, which favours receivers on weaker teams.
stages.distribution: Team volume roughly normal per game; individual share is persistent but shifts with teammate injuries; sack opportunities scale with opponent pass rate.

stages.name: Conversion against remaining opponents
stages.description: Per-opportunity output (yards per carry, yards per target, touchdowns per scoring trip, sacks per pass-rush snap) is adjusted for the remaining opponents' run defense, coverage and pass protection, and for late-season weather in outdoor stadiums. Explosive-play rates matter because one 70-yard run can swing a close yards race.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail for yards (explosive plays); passing TDs and sacks are small-count Poisson-like with overdispersion.

stages.name: Order statistic, ties and settlement
stages.description: End-of-regular-season totals for the full field (including unlisted contenders and teammates who split volume) are compared; the maximum wins, ties split $1/N rounded down, and official stat corrections or provider differences (half sacks, QB sack yardage counted as rushing) can change a close finish. The national series' 'Division I' wording leaves FCS inclusion open.
stages.distribution: Order statistic of correlated overdispersed totals; tie mass material for passing TDs and sacks.

cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.label: Tie probability at the top of a discrete season counting stat
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.mechanism: Probability that two or more players finish the regular season tied for the lead, by stat type: high for passing touchdowns and sacks (small integers; sacks in half units), low for rushing and receiving yards.
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.rationale: Ties pay $1/N rounded down to the cent, so a candidate's expected payout is P(sole leader) + sum over tie sizes of P(tied in N-way) / N. For passing-TD or sack leaders a two-way tie at, say, 11 sacks is a real event, while for yards it is negligible. Ignoring this mis-values both favourites and long shots.
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.measurement: From the joint simulation of end-of-regular-season totals, compute P(max shared by exactly N players) for N = 2, 3. Calibrate by the historical frequency of ties at the top of FBS and power-conference leaderboards for each stat, 2010-2025 regular seasons (NCAA stats), and check the simulation reproduces it within binomial error. Units: probability; sacks evaluated on a 0.5 lattice.
raw_data: player season stats: player, team, conference, stat totals by regular season
historical leaderboards per conference per season
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.why: The $1/N tie payout is part of the contract; passing-TD and sack leader markets have enough tie mass to change fair value.

cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.label: Joint end-of-regular-season simulation of all eligible contenders
cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.mechanism: Monte Carlo of remaining regular-season production for every player in the conference (or FBS) with a realistic chance, including teammates who share usage and players not listed as markets, with team-level shocks shared within a team.
cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.rationale: Leader probability is an order statistic over the whole field. Pricing listed names alone over-states each; teammates (RB1/RB2, two WRs) are negatively correlated through shared usage, while players on the same team share positive shocks from team pace and QB health. Remaining-game counts differ by team (byes already taken, Hawaii 13-game exemption, cancelled games), and conference title games do not count.
cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.measurement: Field = all players within 3 standard deviations of the leader's projected total. For each, per-game production ~ negative binomial (yards: gamma on carries/targets x per-opportunity yards) with mean from leader_race_state and dispersion fitted per position; shared team shock (log-normal SD fitted from team pace residuals) and teammate usage constraint (team carries or targets fixed per simulated game). Remaining games from the official schedule up to the last regular-season week; participation from the hazard input. 20,000 draws; output P(sole leader), P(tied N-way). As-of the prior Sunday.

cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.why: Produces the probability each named player is the regular-season leader given the full field and remaining schedule, which is exactly what each KX...LEADER market settles on.

cfb.leader_race_state.reason: Current total and games remaining dominate late in the season; the input already bundles projection, so the simulation input is kept separate to model the field and ties.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Volume share is the largest driver of rushing and receiving totals; changes after injuries to teammates move it.

cfb.defender_production_profile.reason: Only relevant input for the sacks race; pass-rush snap volume and per-snap sack rate decide it.

cfb.player_participation_hazard.reason: Contract resolves NO if the player does not play; missed games matter more than efficiency shifts in a counting race.

cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.reason: Team dropback pool for passing-TD and receiving leaders.

cfb.dvp.reason: Remaining opponent quality per position shifts per-game means by a meaningful amount over 3-5 games.

cfb.qb_availability_hazard.reason: Receiving leader depends on QB health; irrelevant to sacks race, so secondary.

cfb.player_stat_variance.reason: Dispersion sets catch-up probabilities; captured partly inside the field simulation.

cfb.opt_out_departures.reason: Regular-season sit-outs are rare but happen for redshirt preservation or draft prospects on out-of-contention teams.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Weather shifts pass/run mix in a few remaining games; small cumulative effect.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines scope (regular season, non-conference games count, title games excluded), NO if player does not play, and tie payout.

m.stat_source_mismatch.reason: Official stat corrections after games and provider differences in sacks and rushing can decide close races.

interactions.mechanism: One missed game costs a player about one game of expected production. If the leader's cushion exceeds that, a single absence rarely flips the race; if it is below, a missed game hands the lead over. The effect of injury risk on price therefore jumps around a gap of one game's production.
interactions.how_to_test: In the field simulation, vary the leader's per-game miss probability and plot P(leader) against gap measured in games of production.

interactions.mechanism: Better teams run more plays and score more, raising a feature back's volume, but in blowouts the starter sits for the fourth quarter. Expected season carries rise with team strength and then flatten or fall for heavy favourites, favouring leaders on good-not-dominant teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress per-game carries of top-3 RBs on pregame expected margin with a quadratic term, FBS 2014+.

interactions.mechanism: Expected sacks per game equal pass-rush snaps (driven by opponent dropbacks) times sacks per snap; a top rusher facing two run-heavy service-academy-style opponents gains less than a weaker rusher facing pass-heavy teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Model per-game sacks as Poisson with log-link on log(opponent dropbacks) and rusher rate; test the offset coefficient near 1.

interactions.mechanism: A receiving-yards leader's projection is conditional on his QB: if the starter is lost, team pass yards fall and target concentration may change, so the leader's probability collapses while a rival on a stable team gains.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare receiver per-game yards before and after starting-QB changes, 2014+, controlling for opponent.

interactions.mechanism: For passing TDs and sacks the top of the leaderboard is often bunched within one or two units; the 1/N payout then makes a near-leader's value much higher than P(sole leader) alone, especially with two candidates on a 0.5-sack lattice.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated sole-leader probability versus expected payout including ties by stat type; check historical tie frequencies match.

nonlinearities.shape: sigmoid in gap divided by remaining-production SD
nonlinearities.why: P(lead holds) depends on the standardized gap; with few games left the SD shrinks, so the same yardage gap becomes nearly decisive late but is soft in October.

nonlinearities.shape: step losses of one game of production; absorbing at season-ending injury
nonlinearities.why: Availability does not shade production smoothly: each missed game removes a whole game of volume, and a season-ending injury freezes the total, so its effect on probability is discontinuous.

nonlinearities.shape: lattice spikes for integer and half-integer stats
nonlinearities.why: Passing TDs move in units and sacks in halves, so probability mass concentrates on ties in a way that has no analogue for yards.
